text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Party politics scales first hurdle after voters turn out in large numbers in local elections, Nigeria's first poll on party lines since 1993. Election seen by military government as test of popularity of its programme to restore civilian rule.
- Foreign observers describe local elections as peaceful, democratic and hitch-free. The observers were from a U.S. group dominated by African Americans.
- New management of debt-ridden Nigeria Airways to lay off 1,100 employees as part of measures to rejuvenate the ailing state carrier.
- Local elections marked by large voter turnout but long delays in start of voting.
- Police teargas voters in Onitsha, a commercial city in eastern Nigeria.
- Candidates pushed to the background as people vote for parties rather than candidates; ballot papers bore party symbols, without names or pictures of candidates.

- Exit polls from local elections show the Democratic Party of Nigeria and the United Nigeria Congress Party, two of five legal parties that contested, in the lead. Both parties say they want to adopt military ruler General Sani Abacha as candidate for presidential elections next year to end army rule.

- With closure of its embassy in Nigeria, Canada appears ready to take frosty relations to a logical conclusion. The two Commonealth nations fell out over Canada's championing of sanctions against Nigeria for alleged human rights violations.
